S, THIS DAY, THE COURT MADE THE FOLLOWING:
 -2-  NC: 2024:KHC-D:16485  CRL.P No. 100984 of 2016 CORAM: THE HON'BLE MS. JUSTICE J.M.KHAZI  ORAL ORDER

(PER: THE HON'BLE MS. JUSTICE J.M.KHAZI) Petitioner who is the sole accused has filed this petition under section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure (Cr.P.C.) to quash the criminal proceedings initiated against him in Dharwad Sub-Urban PS crime No.52/2016 for the offences punishable under Sections 406, 465, 468, 471 and 420 IPC.
2.
In support of the petition, the petitioner has contended that the complaint and FIR lodged against him are illegal, baseless and against the principles established by law.
Already the complainant has filed suit claiming her share in the suit schedule properties.
Such being the case, filing of the complaint is unnecessary and unwarranted.
The complainant is trying to convert a civil litigation into criminal proceedings.
The complainant's husband died on 16.06.2004 and a partition deed came to be entered into between the parties on 18.04.2013.
The present NC: 2024:KHC-D:16485 complaint is filed during 2016.
There is inordinate delay in filing the complaint.

Only to harass the petitioner/accused, this complaint is filed and pray to allow the petition and quash the proceedings initiated against him.
3.
Vide order dated 19.09.2016, the further proceedings in this case are stayed.
Thereafter, several adjustments have been granted.

Ultimately, on 13.07.2023, the respondent No.2/complainant has filed the statement of objections stating that the petition is not maintainable and the contention of the petitioner that the dispute between the parties is purely civil in nature is not correct.

The petitioner with the criminal intention of depriving the complainant and her daughter of their rightful shares in the properties has committed impersonation of the deceased husband of the complainant and by forging his sign filed false affidavits/declaration before the public authority for the purpose of creating and producing the false documents NC: 2024:KHC-D:16485 before the public authorities and committed alleged offences.
3.1 The deceased husband of the complainant had separate properties and the complainant and her daughter are entitled to inherit the same.
However, the petitioner has misled the complainant into a partition depriving the properties of her husband.
The complainant and her daughter are allotted meager share, while the joint family is having huge properties.
He has also transferred the motorcycle and shares standing in the name of complainant's husband.
After the said facts came to light, the complainant has filed the complaint.
However, the petitioner by securing stay has totally stalled the investigation.

5. Heard arguments and perused the record.
6.
The relationship between the parties is not in dispute.
Petitioner Shivananda, Basavaraj the husband of complainant and Ujjwala are the children of Hucchanagouda Balotagi.

Unfortunately,
Basavaraj died on 16.06.2004.
He was owning a motorcycle bearing registration No.KA-25 A-5440/Temp.
He was also having 500 shares in Shri Renuka Sugars Ltd.
According to the complainant, E-Schedule properties of O.S.No.461/2014 are the separate properties of her husband Basavaraj.

After the death of Basavaraj, (2009) 7 SCC 495 (2011) 7 SCC 59 (2022) 15 SCC 164 NC:
2024:KHC-D:16485 petitioner has impersonated himself as Basavaraj and transferred the motorcycle to his own name.

The petitioner by giving false information before the revenue authorities has secured heirship certificate by showing the said Basavaraj as unmarried and got his properties transferred to the names of himself.
6.1 After the death of Huchanagouda, the name of the complainant was entered in the records of rights of family properties.

Again, the petitioner in order to deprive the complainant and her daughter of their legitimate share, has given a declaration dated 19.10.2012 by forging the signature of the complainant and based on such documents has got deleted the name of complainant from the said records.
The petitioner has also misled the complainant to enter into a partition deed and allotted meager share to the complainant and her daughter.
7. The complainant and her daughter have filed suit in O.S.No.461/2014 seeking share in the ancestral NC: 2024:KHC-D:16485 properties and also allotment of exclusive properties of Basavaraj to them.
When the complainant realised that petitioner has committed various offences in order to deprive the complainant and her daughter of their legitimate share, she filed the complaint.

8. In support of the allegations made against the petitioner, respondent No.2/complainant has produced the relevant documents, which goes to show that there is prima facie material to conduct detailed investigation.
The allegations made against the petitioner are very serious and they are required to be investigated extensively.
On account of the blanket stay granted on 19.09.2016, there is no progress in the investigation.
It appears, after respondent No.2/complainant has engaged the services of another counsel, they have come up with the application for vacating stay.

9. From the material placed on record, it is evident that even though basically the dispute between the parties is civil in nature, it appears, in order to NC: 2024:KHC-D:16485 deprive the complainant and her daughter of their legitimate share in the family properties, the motorcycle and shares Shivanand Huchanagouda Balotagi vs The State Of Karnataka on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72110371/
3 belonging to Basavaraj, the petitioner is indulged in impersonation and other offences.

sentences.text: Detailed investigation is necessary.
At any stretch of imagination, it cannot be accepted that respondent No.2/complainant is trying to give a civil dispute the colour of criminal nature.
Therefore, the decisions relied upon by the petitioner are not applicable to the case on hand.

10. For the above reasons, this court is of the considered opinion that the petition is devoid of merits and it is liable to be dismissed and accordingly, the following;
ORDER Petition filed by the petitioner/Accused under section 482 Cr.P.C. is dismissed.
